validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki 403'd for both the harvest bot and my own WebFetch, so wiki_citations.json is empty and I could not see what the sheet itself currently cites -- went straight to open-web research per scope notes. This is SSGC's well-documented 'RLNG-2' pipeline, built to carry re-gasified LNG from the Port Qasim/Bin Qasim import terminal in Karachi to the CTS Sawan interconnection with the national gas grid (from Sawan, SNGPL's separate Sawan-Lahore/Sawan-Multan lines, several of which are already other roster rows, e.g. P4090/P4091, carry it north). EXISTENCE: independently confirmed real infrastructure, not GEM-only -- SSGC's own official 'Gas Transmission Capacities Utilization' page names it explicitly as '42in x371 km CTS Bin Qasim to CTS Sawan RLNG-2 Pipeline' with 1200 mmscfd design capacity, and reports it was already receiving/carrying up to 600 mmscfd (i.e. built and operating, ramping toward design capacity) as of 30 June 2018. NS Energy Business (industry trade press, 7 Apr 2017) independently reports the same project: 42in diameter, ~370km CTS Bin Qasim-CTS Sawan, 1.2 bcfd (=1200 mmcfd) capacity, proposed 6 Apr 2017, target completion Oct 2018. These two independent sources agree on diameter (42in, matches GEM Diameter=42.00), length (~370/371km, matches GEM LengthKnown=371.00 exactly against the SSGC page), capacity (1200 mmcfd, matches GEM Capacity=1200.00 exactly), route (Bin Qasim/Karachi -> Sawan, matches GEM Start/EndLocation), proposal timing (2017, matches GEM ProposalYear=2017) and target completion (2018, matches GEM ConstructionYear=2018/StartYear1=2018). SSGC's own site (a separate narrative article, 'How SSGC's RLNG Project will change Pakistan's energy dynamics') also attributes construction/ownership to SSGC alone, consistent with GEM Owner1=Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100%. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a transmission trunk line (moves bulk RLNG from the import terminal to a national-grid interconnection point), not a gathering/feeder line -- confirmed. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 63-row Pakistan-gas roster; the only other Karachi-area/Sindh entries are unrelated older Sui-field networks (e.g. P4014 Nawabshah-Karachi Gas Pipeline, which SSGC's own capacity page separately lists as 'ILBP Nawabshah-Karachi Terminal, 16in x290km, 80 mmscfd' -- a different pipe, matching P4014's own recorded specs exactly, not this one). No roster row shares P3177's 42in/371km/1200mmcfd/Bin Qasim-Sawan signature, so no duplicate/relabel concern. STATUS: 'operating' is well supported -- SSGC's own transmission-network page still lists it as part of the current network, and there is no retirement/decommissioning signal anywhere. One caveat only: SegmentCost is flagged separately below.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM records SegmentCost = $334,000,000 (USD). Independent reporting on this project's cost consistently gives a materially different figure: NS Energy Business (7 Apr 2017) reports SSGC's board conceptually approved Rs64.9 billion ($615.7 million) capital investment for this exact pipeline (42in, ~370km, CTS Bin Qasim-CTS Sawan). The Express Tribune's 2017 headline 'SSGC to pour Rs65b into laying new LNG pipeline' (tribune.com.pk/story/1376611) independently corroborates the ~Rs65 billion figure via its title/snippet, but the article itself 403'd on both WebFetch and url_verifier.py (anti-bot), so I could NOT verify its full content or cite it -- I'm noting it only as directional corroboration, not as a proposed_ref. $615.7M is roughly 1.8x GEM's recorded $334M -- a material disagreement, not a rounding difference, and I found no independent source anywhere that supports the $334M figure specifically. Recommend Update leg re-check the provenance of $334M (possibly a partial/contract-tranche figure, e.g. one of two ~Rs40bn/Rs100bn loan allocations mentioned in reporting, or a stale/miscopied number) before treating $615.7M as a straight replacement.

summary: P3177 (SSGC's RLNG-2 pipeline, Bin Qasim/Karachi->Sawan) confirmed real and correctly classified/attributed/specced (length/diameter/capacity/dates/owner/route all corroborated by SSGC's own capacity-utilization page + NS Energy Business, both verified) -- but SegmentCost ($334M) conflicts with the ~$615.7M (Rs64.9-65bn) reported everywhere else; flagged as an unresolved spec concern, no other issues found.
